notes: Medium. A multi-stage data-tier task: bring a Postgres service up from nothing without systemd (pg_createcluster/pg_ctlcluster), provision app role + database + grants, create a customers table to a prescribed schema, load messy CSVs, and then perform the data cleaning entirely through SQL (lowercase+trim email, digit-only phone, dedupe keeping earliest by (email,phone), delete rows missing both contact fields), persisting load.sql/clean.sql evidence. On top of that the solver must craft and EXERCISE a SQL-injection payload against a naive auth query to authenticate as the admin role, and generate importable grpc python bindings from an arbitrary proto. The verifier re-runs the same /app/solve.py on fresh hidden CSVs (edge/malformed contact rows, dedupe collapse) and fresh protos (renamed packages/services, stream RPCs, enum, oneofes) plus a malformed-proto case that must exit non-zero. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (each later stage depends on the live DB/schema being correct), debugging_ambiguity (postgres bring-up, role/db grants, connection auth, generated-binding imports), hidden_case_generalization (re-run unchanged on fresh fixtures), and reasoning_depth (coordinating SQL cleaning, auth bypass and generic codegen in one undisciplined CLI tool). One container, no GPU/systemd/X; resource pressure is mild.
